title: Composition of finite-type morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the morphism properties [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: locally of finite type is tested on compatible etale scheme charts, and finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact. If $f$ and $g$ are of finite type, then $g\circ f$ is of finite type. No separatedness, representability, finite-presentation, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $P$ for locally of finite type of scheme morphisms. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], $P$ is etale local on source-and-target. Choose a surjective representable etale scheme atlas $W\to Z$. Form $Y_W=Y\times_ZW$, choose a surjective representable etale scheme atlas $V\to Y_W$, form $X_V=X\times_YV$, and choose a surjective representable etale scheme atlas $U\to X_V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A representable map from a scheme is surjective on every scheme base change exactly when its point map is surjective [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so these atlases are singleton etale coverings. Pullback of coverings and composition of etale coverings [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that $V\to Y$ and $U\to X$ are chartwise etale and surjective on point classes; as their sources are schemes they are representable etale, and by the same point criterion they are surjective representable etale. For the last assertion, $U\to X$ factors through $X_V\to X$, the base change of $V\to Y$. Thus we have compatible scheme maps $u:U\to V$ and $v:V\to W$, with $f(U\to X)=(V\to Y)u$ and $g(V\to Y)=(W\to Z)v$. The chart tests in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] give $P(u)$ and $P(v)$, since finite type of $f,g$ includes local finite type.

source.place: Tag 03XG (lemma-composition-finite-type), through Tag 0AML (remark-composition-P); compatible atlases as in Tag 03MJ

proof.text: Apply the locally-of-finite-type clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to the scheme maps $u,v$. It gives $P(vu)$ without any quasi-compactness assumption on these atlas maps. The square with top map $vu:U\to W$, bottom map $gf:X\to Z$, and surjective etale left map $U\to X$ is a presentation diagram. The criterion [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], applied to $P$, which is isomorphism-invariant since local finite type is defined by affine open covers of preimages of affine opens with finitely generated coordinate algebras, which isomorphisms carry to such covers [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with its locality supplied by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], implies that every presentation diagram of $gf$ has locally finite type top map. This is precisely local finite type of $gf$ in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

We prove quasi-compactness using exactly the affine-test convention in [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli], which [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] uses. Fix an affine scheme $T\to Z$ and put $A=Y\times_ZT$, $B=X\times_ZT$. Quasi-compactness of $g$ says that $|A|$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], choose an affine scheme $E$ with a surjective representable etale map $E\to A$. The composite $E\to Y$ is a scheme test for $f$, so $D=X\times_YE$ has quasi-compact point space by quasi-compactness of $f$. There is a canonical isomorphism $D\simeq B\times_AE$: on a test scheme a section on either side is a section of $X$ together with a section of $E$ having the same image in $Y$, since the $T$-coordinate of the $B$-section is forced by that of $E$. Forgetting this forced coordinate and inserting it are inverse and commute with restriction. By pullback of etale coverings [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $D\to B$ is a surjective etale cover. Its point map is surjective and continuous [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus].

source.place: Tags 03HE (definition-quasi-compact), 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), transitivity hint expanded with affine tests

proof.text: To check compactness of $|B|$ explicitly, pull an arbitrary open cover of $|B|$ back along $|D|\to|B|$. Continuity makes this an open cover of $|D|$, which has a finite subcover. Surjectivity implies that the corresponding finitely many original opens cover $|B|$. Thus the pullback of $gf$ over every affine $T\to Z$ has quasi-compact point space. The definition [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli] therefore makes $gf$ quasi-compact. Combining this with step 2 gives finite type of $gf$ by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. The construction also covers empty spaces: the affine atlas of an empty $A$ can be empty, and compactness and surjectivity above remain valid.
